issue.title: Autouse _isolate_sase_home allocates per-test homes with quadratic TempPathFactory.mktemp scans
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-1q4.3 note #2 (epic sase-1q4, kwonly_core phase, 2026-10-30): the primary
scoped `sase tool run check` spent over two hours inside pytest
`TempPathFactory.mktemp("home")`, whose `popen-gw0` basetemp directory held 27,816
entries at the time.

Root cause (confirmed by reading the code on master 4a4b6fede8):

- `tests/_conftest_environment.py::_isolate_sase_home` is an autouse fixture that calls
  `tmp_path_factory.mktemp("home")` once per test.
- `_pytest/pathlib.py::make_numbered_dir` computes the next suffix with
  `max(map(parse_num, find_suffixes(root, prefix)))`, which lists the whole basetemp
  root on every call.
- So each test pays O(entries in basetemp), and a worker that runs N tests pays O(N^2)
  directory scanning; with ~28k entries per worker every allocation lists ~28k entries.

Suggested remedy: allocate the fake home from a bounded/session-scoped allocator (for
example one session-scoped base dir plus `tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=base)` or a per-worker
counter) so per-test cost is O(1); keep homes outside each test's own `tmp_path`, and
measure `just check` / `just test` runtime before and after.

task_type_fields.impact:
Every pytest worker slows down quadratically with the number of tests it runs; on a long
lane this stretched one agent's scoped check past two hours, and it inflates every
`just check` / CI test lane run on the shared host.
